entries.complaint: The example 'Junction.ID' is ambiguous about whether the query parser expects the literal English scope name 'Junction', or accepts a localized element name the way it accepts translated AND/OR (per prompt_context_by_prefix). I rendered it as 'जंक्शन.ID', translating the scope word to match the app's own element-name vocabulary and keeping ID as-is (ID is an exempt key elsewhere in this sprint). If the parser only recognizes the literal English token 'Junction', this example is now wrong and would mislead a user typing a query.
readings: Scope names are translated like AND/OR, so 'जंक्शन.ID' is correct
Scope names are literal parser keywords and the example must keep 'Junction.ID' even in translation

entries.complaint: The English value 'Mapbox DEM' is not in this sprint's exempt_keys, so lang_syntax_validate.php flags it identical-to-English if left unchanged. I transliterated the brand name to 'मैपबॉक्स DEM' to pass the check. The es translator hit the identical problem on this same key and used a different fix (word reorder), and noted that several other already-shipped language files still carry the byte-identical 'Mapbox DEM' string for this key -- suggesting either those files are failing this check unnoticed, or a brand-name-plus-acronym string like this one needs its own exemption category rather than each translator improvising a different workaround.
readings: Add this shape of string (brand name + acronym) to a standing exemption category
Each language keeps improvising its own fix, and drift between languages is accepted

entries.complaint: This tip and lpn_run_menu_tip / lpn_time_no_period name controls (Time menu, Calculate button, Total run time, Settings, Calculation, Hydraulics) whose own keys (lpn_time_menu, lpn_time_run, lpn_time_duration, lpn_menu_settings, lpn_settings_sec_calculation, and the Hydraulics section heading) are not yet translated into Hindi at all, so those controls currently render in English on screen. I therefore left those control names in English inside the Hindi sentence to match what a Hindi-reading user actually sees on the button/menu, rather than inventing a Hindi phrase that would point at nothing. If those sibling keys are translated in a future sprint, these three strings will need a follow-up pass to translate the same words.
readings: Leave the untranslated control names in English until their own keys are translated (what I did)
Translate them now anyway, accepting a temporary mismatch with the still-English control
